# Motion model evaluation

<!-- Generated by sifted_motion_eval (eval/sifted_motion_eval.cpp). Do not edit by hand. -->

Legacy estimator against the IMM (ADR 0014), side by side on the same inputs. Reproduce from the repository root (the Monte Carlo sets are regenerated, never committed):

```bash
cmake --preset release && cmake --build --preset release
(cd sim && python3 -m sifted_sim.manoeuvres evaluation ../build/release/manoeuvres-eval)
build/release/eval/sifted_motion_eval --scenarios build/release/manoeuvres-eval --scenarios tests/fixtures/scenarios --title "Motion model evaluation" --out docs/motion-model-evaluation.md
```

## Models compared

| | `cv` (legacy) | `imm` (default since ADR 0014) |
|---|---|---|
| state | `[px, py, vx, vy]` | the same, in each of three modes |
| motion | one constant-velocity model, white-noise acceleration q = 4 m^2/s^3, x10 while a fading-memory NIS detector reports a manoeuvre | quiet / manoeuvre / hard constant-velocity modes, switched by a continuous-time Markov chain |
| update | Joseph-form EKF | Joseph-form EKF per mode, each linearised at its own state; log-space mode likelihoods |
| gate and cost | d^2 under the filter's prediction | the mixture statistic over the modes (ADR 0014) |
| reported estimate | the filter's | the moment-matched combination of the modes |

Everything else (gate probability, global nearest neighbour, lifecycle, sensors) is the same. Old recordings replay with `cv`.

## Method

117 scenario runs per model. The manoeuvre set (`manoeuvre_<load>g_<speed>mps`, 10 noise seeds each, `sim/sifted_sim/manoeuvres.py`): one radar at the origin (10 m, 0.2 deg, 1 Hz, Pd 0.9, 0.5 clutter points per scan, 60 km), one target from (-6000, 15000) m flying east: 30 s straight, a right turn of min(180 deg / rate, 40 s), 30 s straight. Its seeds and turn profiles are disjoint from the tuning set the parameters were checked on (ADR 0014).

`cv`: the legacy constant-velocity filter with NIS-switched process noise. `imm`: the IMM (ADR 0014) with q = 0.50 / 25.0 / 1200 m^2/s^3, sojourn 60 / 30 / 15 s. Direct engine feed, default configuration otherwise. Per condition, averages over its runs: ID switches and false tracks per run, missed target-instants (mean of per-run percentages), mean per-target position and velocity RMSE.

Metrics follow the scorecard (CLEAR-MOT style, 100 m match distance; eval/sifted/eval/scenario.hpp). An ID switch is a target matched to a different track than before, usually because the original track lost the target and a new one was started. A missed target-instant is a covered target with no matched track. At 15-25 km one radar measurement's cross-range error is 50-90 m, so part of the remaining misses are instants where the estimate is further than 100 m from the truth. NEES and NIS test the reported covariance (below). The fixture rows are single noise realisations; the Monte Carlo evaluation ([evaluation-monte-carlo.md](evaluation-monte-carlo.md)) scores them over many.

Phases come from the truth: `turn` when the true velocity changes by more than 0.5 m/s^2, `onset` / `exit` the first 10 s of a turn / of the straight flight after it.

## Findings

- **Identity through 3 g at 100 m/s:** at most 0.4 ID switches per run with `imm`, 2.7 with `cv`. Target (at most about 0.2): **not met**; `imm` first exceeds it at 3.0 g.
- **Identity through 3 g at 250 m/s:** at most 0.4 ID switches per run with `imm`, 6.8 with `cv`. Target (at most about 0.2): **not met**; `imm` first exceeds it at 3.0 g.
- **Fixtures:** `imm` has the lower mean position RMSE on 7 of 7 single-realisation fixtures.
- **Consistency:** in turns NEES4 goes from 32.4 to 2.7 (expected 4). In straight flight it goes from 2.57 to 2.10: the IMM does not make straight flight honest. The simulator's straight legs have exactly zero acceleration, so any filter that budgets for manoeuvres is pessimistic there, and the mixed-in manoeuvre modes add to that budget (docs/design.md section 7).

## Costs, measured elsewhere

- **Compute:** per-scan time, throughput and tracks per core for both estimators on the same machine: [benchmarks.md](benchmarks.md).
- **Clutter:** the IMM confirms more false tracks than a constant-velocity tracker as clutter rises: [evaluation-baseline.md](evaluation-baseline.md) and [evaluation-monte-carlo.md](evaluation-monte-carlo.md).
- **Dense formations and gating:** identity in a 45 m formation over re-seeded fixtures, the gating statistics compared on separate selection sets, and the engine-level loss rate on the IMM's own matched model: [ADR 0014](adr/0014-imm-motion-model.md) and `ConsistencyMonteCarlo.ImmMatchedModelIsNearlyConsistent`.
